chapter: Hippolyte Charles, the bass and other bands
title: Jules Batiste, Johnny St. Cyr and playing with Robichaux
summary: Dawson knew of Jules Batiste, praises guitarist Johnny St. Cyr, and says he played guitar in John Robichaux's full band before St. Cyr did.

blocks.x: Did you ever know two guys, they called themselves Jack and Jill? Uh... Jack Dowden, he played mandolin. And Jules Batiste, he played guitar?

Oh, Jules Batiste. I heard of him, but that's been nice, a good while now. Yeah. Johnny St. Cyr used to play with him. Johnny St. Cyr was, uh... Was a guitar player too. A fine guitar player too. Yeah. Johnny St. Cyr was... Well, he complimented. He played with Brobyshire's band too, used to... He played with all them, uh... all them big high bands.

Yeah, I know Robichaux. I played with him a couple of times in his band. Oh, really? Yeah. I played... I played with Robichaux before he... Before Johnny St. Cyr got there. They got... Robichaux had a... had a full band. Uh-huh. And I played with playing guitar then. Robichaux had me on the guitar, I started playing, uh... Rice and... What do you know? On, uh... Iberville, a little before my race. He was playing, and he used to go in the country too. He had more, I see here. That's Aunt Benson. How long you had that?
